free_tier.stated: 400 MB per week, reset Sunday 19:00 CET: 'Upload up to 400 MB of music each week for free' and 'Your weekly upload quota of 400 MB is automatically reset every Sunday at 7:00 pm (CET)'. ~1.7 GB/month recurring, uncapped total accumulation.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: No retention clause documented in available terms.

egress.terms: Free streaming; no per-GB egress charge. 'Podcast and RSS Feed for your Profile and Sets of music' is included on the free side, which is unusual.

tooling: No API. Web upload plus a 'Sounds import from sharehosters' feature (pull from a sharehoster URL rather than uploading through the browser). That is the automation-adjacent path.
chaining: 400 MB/week x N accounts, accumulating indefinitely (the quota resets, storage does not expire). ~1.7 GB/month/account at zero cost, so 10 accounts is ~17 GB/month and 100 accounts ~170 GB/month. Throughput, not quota, is the constraint.
limits_note: 400 MB/week on Free; transcode to a single house format. 'We convert all uploaded tracks to a unified streaming format: 192 kbit/s, constant bitrate (CBR), joint stereo'; Premium can pick bitrate and gets 'original (mp3 only)' play quality.

identity_cost.detail: no identity_cost field and no identity statement in the source record; defaulted to email and flagged, not evidence

reliability_note: RE-ENCODES to 192 kbps CBR joint stereo for everyone on Free ('This ensures compatibility across all devices. Premium members can set their own bitrate preferences'). The 'original (mp3 only)' option in the feature list is a Premium/paid capability, so on the free tier what comes out is the 192k transcode, not your file.
